articles.title: Court orders Jimmy Odukoya to appear Thursday over church dispute
articles.summary:
The Lagos State High Court has directed the Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, to appear before it on Thursday, November 26, over the ongoing leadership crisis in the church.

Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin gave the directive on Monday after hearing an application by the church’s counsel, Ibitayo Reju, seeking permission to serve Odukoya with court processes through substituted means.

The court granted the application by the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, allowing the service of Form 48, the originating court processes, orders and notices through newspaper publication, pasting at Odukoya’s last known address in Ilupeju, Lagos, and electronic means.

The enrolled order stated: “Leave is hereby granted to the Applicant to serve Form 48, the originating court process to be filed in this suit, Orders made, Notices issued, and all other processes to be issued and filed in this suit on the Respondent through substituted means by newspaper publication in several newspaper that is in wide circulation within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court and by pasting at a conspicuous part of the Respondent’s last known address at No. 12 Industrial Estate Road, off Town Planning Way, Ilupeju, Lagos State and also through any Electronical means.”

The judge also directed Odukoya to be present in court on the adjourned date to show cause.

“The Respondent is required to be present in Court on the said date,” the order stated.

The case was subsequently adjourned until November 26, 2026.

The latest development is part of the dispute over the church’s leadership following the purported removal of Odukoya as its Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

Odukoya had earlier instituted a separate suit at the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees, including his purported removal from office.

The leadership crisis also led to an earlier order by the Lagos State High Court on November 18, restraining him from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.

However, during Sunday’s service at the church in Ilupeju, Lagos, Odukoya told the congregation that although he had heard about the injunction, he had not been formally served with the court order.

“I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said.

His comments followed a visit by the founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, who urged church members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu.

The post Court orders Jimmy Odukoya to appear Thursday over church dispute appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Police arrest 10 suspected cultists, four kidnappers, others in Edo
articles.summary:
The Edo State Police Command has arrested ten suspected cultists, one armed robbery suspect, four suspected kidnappers and one murder suspect in intensified operations against violent crimes across the state.

The arrests were disclosed by the Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), ASP Eno Ikoedem, on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, during a Monday press briefing in Benin City.

According to the command, the arrests underscore its determination to sustain pressure on criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents.

In one operation, the police arrested a suspected armed robber at Ugiokhuen Community, recovering a locally fabricated pistol, ammunition and other exhibits.

The command also recorded a major breakthrough in a kidnapping incident reported on November 19, with the rescue of two victims, Yakubu Ibrahim and Abdullahi Mohammed, unhurt, and the arrest of four suspected kidnappers during an intensive bush-combing operation at Ikakumoh/Ayaran Forest.

Furthermore, four members of the Edo State Security Corps were arrested for allegedly leaking information on police movements to suspected cultists, thereby frustrating an ongoing operation.

In a separate anti-cultism operation at Osakpolor Street, off Adolor College Road, Benin City, ten suspected members of the Aye Axe cult group were arrested during an alleged initiation exercise, while a Mercedes-Benz GLK 350 was recovered.

The command also arrested one John Bello, who allegedly murdered his father, Julius Bello, in Fugar and fled, before he was subsequently tracked down and apprehended.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Patrick Daaor, reiterated the command’s resolve to dismantle criminal networks and bring perpetrators to justice.

He commended the officers involved for their courage and professionalism, and appreciated members of the public for their timely information and continued support.

Residents were urged to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities, as the security of Edo State remains a collective responsibility.

The post Police arrest 10 suspected cultists, four kidnappers, others in Edo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Delta killings: Keyamo condemns attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team
articles.summary:
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the attack on the campaign team of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State, which reportedly left four people dead and four others critically injured.

Keyamo described the incident as disturbing and called on security agencies to identify and arrest those responsible for the killings.

The attack occurred on Monday in the Uduere area of Ughelli North Local Government Area while Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central, was on a campaign tour of the community.

Sunny Areh, the former senator’s media adviser, said armed men opened fire on Omo-Agege’s entourage at close range as he addressed supporters. He added that Omo-Agege escaped unhurt.

Those reportedly killed in the attack were identified as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, while the injured included Evance Ivwurie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba and Ayodo Wanogho.

In a statement issued on Monday, Keyamo linked the incident to what he described as an increasingly hostile political atmosphere in the state.

He also recalled the killing of a tricycle operator in a daylight attack in Asaba on November 7, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents.

“I call on the law enforcement agencies to fish out the perpetrators of these killings, both in Asaba and Ughelli, and bring them to book,” he said.

The minister said he had been engaging senior security officials over the rising incidents of political violence and inflammatory statements in Delta State.

He noted that political disagreements in the state had largely remained peaceful since 1999, expressing concern that political competition was now being accompanied by threats and violence.

“We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is absolutely no need for a descent into violence,” Keyamo said.

He specifically criticised the use of the phrase “Rig and Die”, which he said had contributed to tensions in the state and elsewhere.

“Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country,” he said.

Keyamo also warned political leaders against encouraging supporters to attack opponents or other citizens, insisting that the responsibility for dealing with offenders rested with law enforcement agencies.

“It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” he added.

The minister appealed to Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to address residents and caution individuals making threats of violence.

He said the governor, as the state’s chief security officer, should urgently speak to the people and warn those threatening to cause violence.

The statement comes weeks after Omo-Agege made remarks about the 2027 general election, warning that anyone caught rigging the poll could be killed.

Speaking in October, the former deputy senate president said, “Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him! If you don’t value your life, come and rig the election.”

He also declared, “It is rig and die. We’re going to give them aura for aura. There’s no court this time. We’re going to fight.”

The post Delta killings: Keyamo condemns attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: 2027: Falana warns politicians against violence ahead of elections
articles.summary:
Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) and human rights activist, Femi Falana, has warned that political violence and killings ahead of the 2027 general elections will continue unless perpetrators are swiftly arrested and prosecuted.

Falana said the failure to hold those responsible for previous election-related violence accountable had encouraged impunity and emboldened political actors to resort to violence.

He spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday while reacting to recent election-related incidents, including the killing of four supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State.

The human rights lawyer described the deaths as tragic and preventable, arguing that people would think twice before engaging in violence if they knew they would face the full weight of the law.

“The stakes are high for the political class, but in this unfortunate incident, nothing may come of it. Yesterday, we lost scores of people in Bayelsa State in what was a boat accident. What would happen? Donations have already started; who is the owner of the boat?

“Nobody would have thought they were going to kill people in a rally if they know that the law will catch up with them,” Falana said.

He urged the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), civil society organisations and human rights groups to take a more active role in addressing the country’s political challenges rather than leaving the responsibility entirely to politicians.

“Arrests may be made in Delta State, but I am challenging the Nigerian Bar Association and the human rights community to intervene very decisively because if we leave the affairs of our country in the hands of politicians, we will run into a serious crisis,” he said.

Falana also called on the NBA to mobilise lawyers to assist the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in prosecuting electoral offenders.

He argued that the commission was already burdened with pre-election and post-election litigation and needed support to ensure that electoral offences did not go unpunished.

Beyond political violence, the senior lawyer called for greater public scrutiny of the electoral process, including the cleaning up of the voters’ register, accountability by electoral officials and transparent transmission of election results.

He also urged political parties and candidates to focus their campaigns on governance and issues affecting Nigerians rather than relying on ethnic and religious divisions.

Falana identified unspent funds allocated to basic education by state governments, compulsory health insurance, implementation of child rights laws, fuel subsidy controversies, crude oil-backed loans and stalled refinery rehabilitation projects as issues that should feature prominently in political debates.

Despite his concerns about the country’s political climate, he said Nigeria was not beyond redemption, insisting that existing laws could bring about meaningful change if citizens, the media and civil society organisations demanded accountability.

“So for me it’s not a hopeless situation. It is about promoting debates and that’s what I miss,” he said, urging Nigerians to engage political leaders on substantive national issues rather than focus only on political campaigns and spectacles.

The post 2027: Falana warns politicians against violence ahead of elections appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: 2027: Omo-Agege predicts Peter Obi’s victory, says APC has no chance in Delta
articles.summary:
Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has dismissed the possibility of the All Progressives Congress (APC) securing electoral victories in Delta State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He maintained that Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), enjoys widespread support across the state.

Omo-Agege stated this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, following his escape from an alleged assassination attempt.

He declared that the APC had “no chance” of winning any election in Delta State.

“Peter Obi remains very popular here in Delta State. There is no chance that APC will win anything,” he said.

“Peter Obi won here in 2023, and he did so without an agent; he did so without Omo-Agege, he did so without others. He remains very popular here, and a combination of my support base and Obi’s own support base here in Delta State; there’s no chance that APC will have anything, and they know that,” he said.

Recall that Omo-Agege was once the biggest APC leader in Delta when he was Deputy Senate President and governorship candidate in 2023.

In May 2026, Omo-Agege left the APC and joined the NDC.

On 30th May 2026, at the NDC national convention, he seconded the nomination of Peter Obi as the presidential candidate of the party

articles.title: Delta killings: Obi demands justice for slain NDC supporters
articles.summary:
Former Governor of Anambra state, Peter Obi, has condemned the killing of four supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State, calling on security agencies to investigate the attack and bring those responsible and their sponsors to justice.

Obi also urged the authorities to strengthen security around political activities and protect Nigerians exercising their democratic rights, warning against the growing violence targeting opposition supporters.

He made the call in a statement posted on his X handle following an attack involving former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, and his supporters in Delta State.

Describing the killings as a senseless act of violence, the NDC Presidential candidate expressed concern over what he described as repeated attacks on opposition supporters across the country.

“It is no longer sufficient for those responsible to fund the dissemination of false claims against the opposition.

“They have now escalated to the appalling practice of murdering innocent Nigerians solely because of their political affiliations,” he said.

Obi identified the deceased as Hon. Moses Anaughe, immediate past Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission; Comrade Akima Efenena Umukoro, former President of the Urhobo Progress Union Youth Wing; and Nyoren Okoro, an NDC chieftain. The identity of the fourth victim had yet to be established.

He said 15 other people sustained critical injuries and were receiving medical attention. Among them were Hon. Evance Ivwurie, chairman of Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation, and Comrade Chuks Erhire, its director-general.

Obi commiserated with the families of the deceased and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured, while insisting that the incident must be thoroughly investigated.

“I urge the security agencies to conduct a comprehensive investigation, identify those responsible and their sponsors, and ensure they face justice,” he said.

He stressed that Nigerians had a constitutional right to support political parties and candidates of their choice without intimidation or fear of violence.

“Political differences must be resolved through persuasion and the ballot, never through the use of bullets. No political ambition is worth the life of even one Nigerian,” Obi added.

articles.title: 2027 Elections: IGP to meet with party chairmen, secretaries over political violence, others
articles.summary:
From Molly Kilete, Abuja

Ahead of the 2027, general elections, the Inspector General of Police(IGP), Olatunji Disu, will on Tuesday, meet with chairmen and secretaries of all the political parties in the country.

The meeting/interactive session is schedule to take place at the Goodluck Ebele Jonathan Peacekeeping Hall, Force Headquarters, Abuja.

Top on the agenda of the meeting schedule for 11;o’clock in the morning according to a letter of invitation by the force public relations officer Ani Iniedu, will focus on “political violence, campaign-related violence, destruction of campaign banners and other campaign materials, as well as the disruption of political campaigns and rallies by political thugs”.

The meeting with the leaders of the political parties it was gathered had become necessary following attack on innocent persons during campaigns.

Aside the concerns listed for deliberations, the meeting it was gathered will also focus on hate speech which has become the other of the day by some politicians.

A security source who does not want to be mentioned in print, told Daily Sun, that security reports at the disposal of the security agencies revealed that the elections may be marred with severe violence that may overwhelm the security agencies to curtail if nothing is done at this early stage to address some of the ugly incidences that could trigger a breakdown of law and order before, during and after the ejections.

Already most of the chairmen, secretaries and other leaders of all the political parties have arrived Abuja for the meeting.

Some of the leaders who spoke to Daily Sun, described the meeting as timely and commendable and expressed the hope that the outcome of decisions reached would end the violence and unnecessary attacks especially on the opposition parties at the end of the day.

articles.title: FG declares war on oil thieves, drug barons, arraigns oil boss, 7 others
articles.summary:
The Federal Government has stepped up its war against economic and drug-related crimes, arraigning an oil entrepreneur and seven others over alleged illegal dealings in petroleum products while unveiling measures to fast-track drug trafficking trials and confiscate proceeds of illicit activities.

The two developments in Abuja yesterday signalled the government’s renewed push to dismantle criminal networks through speedy prosecution, asset recovery and stronger collaboration among law enforcement agencies, prosecutors, the judiciary and international partners.

Chairman of Ebenco Group Limited, Ebenezer Oluwagbemiga, was arraigned alongside seven other defendants before Justice Binta Nyako of the Federal High Court, Abuja, on a five-count charge bordering on alleged dealings in petroleum products without lawful authority or the requisite licence.

The other defendants are Elliot Boukoru, Peter Nzekwo, MV Ebenco Grace IMO-7239759, Ebenco Global Link Limited, MT ROSE IMO-8106795, Florence Marine and Shipping Limited, and Ganiyu Basit Olatunbosun.

All the defendants pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Rotimi Oyedepo, who led the prosecution, told the court that the five-count charge was filed on November 3 and urged it to take the defendants’ pleas.

“There is a charge of five counts filed on Nov. 3. We prayed that my lord accept the charge and cause the plea of the defendants to be taken,” he said.

Following their pleas, Oyedepo urged the court to grant an accelerated hearing, citing the economic implications of the alleged offences.

“Considering the sensitivity of the matter and the implications on the economy, we urge the honourable court to grant an accelerated hearing,” he said.

The prosecution also sought an order remanding the defendants in custody pending the determination of the case or as the court might deem appropriate.

However, counsel to the first, second, third, fourth, fifth and eighth defendants, Femi Falana, informed the court that bail applications had been filed for the first, second, third and eighth defendants.

He added that the defence had responded to the prosecution’s counter-affidavits through replies on points of law.

Olalekan Ojo appeared for the sixth and seventh defendants.

Justice Nyako adjourned the matter until November 24 at 1 p.m. for hearing of the bail applications and ordered that the defendants remain in the custody of the arresting agency pending the hearing.

The prosecution said the alleged offences contravened provisions of the Miscellaneous Offences Act, Cap. M17, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, including Section 3(6), and are punishable under Section 1(17) of the Act.

Meanwhile, Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, has announced plans to strengthen the prosecution of drug-related offences through speedy trials, confiscation of criminal assets and increased international cooperation.

Speaking at the inauguration of the National Drug Control Master Plan (NDCMP) 2026–2030 in Abuja, Fagbemi said the Federal Ministry of Justice would work with the judiciary to ensure the speedy disposal of drug-related cases in line with the Administration of Criminal Justice Act.

He said the government would also intensify efforts to strip convicted traffickers of the proceeds of their crimes, warning that criminal networks must not be allowed to enjoy the financial benefits of their illegal activities.

“The government will intensify mutual legal assistance, extradition processes and cross-border asset recovery to disrupt the financial networks sustaining organised drug trafficking.

“These measures are necessary to strengthen Nigeria’s criminal justice response and ensure that drug traffickers did not continue to benefit from the proceeds of their illegal activities,” he said.

The minister said prosecution and asset recovery remained critical to dismantling organised criminal enterprises, particularly those operating across international borders.

He commended the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) for strengthening cooperation between investigators and prosecutors from the early stages of criminal investigations, noting that the approach had improved evidence gathering, reduced procedural errors and enhanced the prosecution of drug cases.

Fagbemi described the agency as central to Nigeria’s drug control efforts, commending its Chairman, Buba Marwa, for his contributions to the fight against drug trafficking and substance abuse.

“The agency remains the bedrock of our national drug control architecture, delivering vital results across intelligence operations, interdiction, investigation, prosecution and public sensitisation.

“I specifically commend Buba Marwa, who has been a silent achiever and has consistently made this administration and country proud,” he said.

The Attorney-General, however, stressed that the government’s tougher prosecution strategy would distinguish between major drug traffickers and persons suffering from substance use disorders.

He said drug kingpins should face the full weight of the law, while persons struggling with drug dependence should receive medical treatment, psychological support and rehabilitation.

According to him, an effective national drug control policy must combine law enforcement with prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration.

Fagbemi said the NDCMP 2026–2030 was designed to strengthen cooperation among law enforcement agencies, public health institutions, educational authorities, social development agencies, financial investigators and community organisations.

He also praised the NDLEA’s alternative development initiatives aimed at encouraging communities involved in illicit drug cultivation to embrace legitimate agricultural activities.

He said the initiative, which promotes the cultivation of lawful cash crops in place of illicit drugs, was consistent with President Bola Tinubu’s agenda of turning challenges into opportunities for progress.

The minister urged relevant institutions to translate the provisions of the master plan into measurable programmes, insisting that it must guide their daily operations rather than remain a policy document without practical impact.

The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Commission has pledged support for Nigeria’s new drug control strategy, describing it as a significant contribution to regional efforts against drug trafficking and substance abuse.

ECOWAS Commissioner for Human Development and Social Affairs, Nassirou Bako-Arifari, said the success of the master plan would depend on sustained political commitment, adequate funding and cooperation among governments, civil society organisations, communities and international partners.

He noted that the cross-border nature of drug trafficking made coordinated action among West African countries imperative.

“Nigeria’s progress in implementing the master plan will contribute significantly to strengthening regional cooperation against illicit drug trafficking and its associated consequences.

“The ECOWAS Commission will stand with Nigeria at every step, sharing experience, mobilising support and linking this national effort to the work of other member states.

“Nigeria’s progress will guide the region because no country can win this fight alone,” he said.

articles.title: INEC chairman, Sowore clash over subpoena as trial stalls
articles.summary:
The failure of the African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, to file court documents within the stipulated time stalled proceedings yesterday his ongoing trial over alleged cybercrime offences before the Federal High Court, Abuja.

Sowore’s lawyer, Reuben Adakole, who represented him when the case was last heard on November 17, had undertaken to file his client’s response before the next adjourned date.

The response was to address an application filed by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan (SAN), seeking to set aside a subpoena issued on him at the instance of the defendant.

The politician is being prosecuted by the Department of State Services (DSS) over social media posts he allegedly published on X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook in August 2025, in which he described President Bola Tinubu as a “criminal” and accused him of lying about the level of corruption in the country.

When the matter was called on Monday, Sowore’s lawyer, Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika (SAN), told the court that his colleagues were experiencing difficulties filing the defendant’s counter-affidavit at the court registry.

Olumide-Fusika explained that he was informed that officials responsible for generating Remita payment details at the registry were experiencing technical difficulties.

He consequently sought a short stand-down to enable his colleagues to complete the filing process.

However, Amupitan’s lawyer, Alex Izinyon (SAN), expressed disappointment over the defence team’s decision to wait until Monday to file its response, insisting that the documents ought to have been filed earlier.

Izinyon recalled that at the previous sitting on November 17, Adakole had undertaken to file the defendant’s response before the next hearing date, questioning why the defence waited until the day of the hearing.

He further disclosed that rather than file the expected response, the defendant opted to file a notice of preliminary objection, which was served on him last Friday.

According to him, the development forced him to work throughout the weekend to prepare a reply, which he filed before the court commenced sitting on Monday and subsequently served on the defence.

While the lawyers were still deliberating on how to proceed, Justice Mohammed Umar suggested that the matter be adjourned until Tuesday.

However, shortly after the suggestion, one of Olumide-Fusika’s colleagues rushed into the courtroom with the newly filed documents, prompting the defence lawyer to hand a copy to Izinyon.

After examining the documents, Izinyon confirmed that they contained a counter-affidavit and a written address.

He, however, told the court that he would need time to study the processes and file a response, either before the court registry closed on Monday or early Tuesday before the commencement of proceedings.

Following the absence of any objection from the prosecuting counsel, Akinlolu Kehinde (SAN), Justice Umar adjourned the matter until Tuesday for hearing.

The counter-affidavit and preliminary objection filed by Sowore are responses to Amupitan’s application seeking to set aside the subpoena issued at the defendant’s instance.

Sowore wants the INEC chairman to appear in court as his witness and produce certain documents, including the academic credentials President Tinubu submitted to the electoral commission.

At the last sitting, Izinyon had argued that the subpoena should be set aside on the grounds of alleged irregularities.

He also faulted the claim by Sowore’s lawyer, Adakole, that his client had filed an application seeking to amend the subpoena.

Izinyon argued that the defence could not introduce another application to amend the subpoena without first addressing the alleged irregularities surrounding the original process.

He further maintained that Adakole needed to clarify whether Sowore intended to withdraw the original subpoena or proceed with the application to amend it.

The INEC chairman’s lawyer insisted that the subpoena could not be altered at Sowore’s instance without a proper order of the court.

Ukraine and Germany reach preliminary agreement on additional interceptor missiles for Ukraine
articles.summary:
Ukrainian Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara and his German counterpart Boris Pistorius discussed ways to strengthen Ukraine's air defences ahead of winter and reached preliminary agreements on additional interceptor missiles for Ukraine during a meeting in Berlin on 23 November.

Source: European Pravda, citing the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine

Details: The main topic of the meeting between the two ministers was increasing support for Ukraine ahead of winter, particularly strengthening its air defences.

Specifically, they focused on steps to secure additional interceptor missiles. The Defence Ministry stressed that the ministers had reached "preliminary agreements in this area".

They also separately discussed cooperation between the two countries' defence industries, drone procurement for Ukraine in 2027 and the scaling up of solutions proven on the battlefield.

The ministers also discussed sharing expertise. The Defence Ministry noted that Ukraine is developing programmes that will enable it to share the country's practical experience of modern warfare and combat-proven technological solutions with its partners.

Background:

On 17 November, it was reported that Germany and Norway would jointly finance a new military aid package for Ukraine under the
PURL
the Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL), a US-NATO programme under which NATO allies purchase US-made weapons for Ukraine
initiative for purchasing US weapons. The package will focus on PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles for Patriot air defence systems, with Berlin contributing US$300 million.

On 4 November, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy discussed the purchase of PAC-2 missiles and ammunition for F-16 fighter jets with Pistorius.

On 7 November, Pistorius stated that Germany could no longer supply Patriot systems to Ukraine from its own stocks, as doing so would create gaps in Germany's defences.

articles.title: Russians attack three districts of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast with drones, injuring two men in Pavlohrad
articles.summary:
Russian forces have attacked three districts of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast with drones, injuring two men in Pavlohrad.

Source: Oleksandr Hanzha, Head of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast Military Administration, in his morning report on 24 November

Quote: "A fire has broken out in Pavlohrad. Two men aged 29 and 36 have been injured. They are receiving outpatient treatment."

Details: Hanzha said the Russians had attacked the Pavlohrad, Samar and Nikopol districts with drones.

They damaged storage facilities in the Pishchanka
hromada
A hromada is an administrative unit designating a village, several villages, or a town, and their adjacent territories
in the Samar district. The city of Nikopol and the Marhanets hromada in the Nikopol district came under attack.

Background: Russian forces struck infrastructure facilities, warehouses, a petrol station and residential buildings across six districts of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on 23 November.

articles.title: Russian forces attack Vinnytsia twice: fire breaks out, one person injured
articles.summary:
Russian forces have attacked the city of Vinnytsia twice on 24 November. A fire broke out following the first attack, while the second struck a critical infrastructure facility, injuring one person, according to early reports.

Source: Vinnytsia Mayor Serhii Morhunov; Ukraine's Air Force

Update: During the second attack, the Russians struck a critical infrastructure facility. Morhunov said a trolleybus and a car had been damaged.

Quote from Morhunov: "According to early reports, one person has been injured. Emergency services are working at the scene."

Details: An explosion was heard in Vinnytsia during the first attack. According to early reports from Morhunov, the fire broke out after a Russian drone was shot down. Firefighters were at the scene. No one was injured.

The Air Force reported earlier that a jet-powered drone was heading towards Nemyriv in Vinnytsia Oblast. The military subsequently indicated that it was heading towards "Tyvriv/Vinnytsia".

articles.title: Russian forces attack Zaporizhzhia, killing two people and injuring 40 – photos
articles.summary:
Russian forces have attacked the city of Zaporizhzhia, killing two people and injuring 40, including a baby, two young children and a 16-year-old girl.

Source: Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration; Ivan Fedorov, co-chair of Zaporizhzhia Oblast Defence Council

Update: Semikin reported that the number of people injured had risen from 32 to 40.

Damage caused by Russia
Photo: Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration

Details: A baby, two children aged 4 and 6 and a 16-year-old girl are among those injured.

Semikin initially reported that 11 people had been injured. He said that one woman was in a serious condition with blast injuries and a traumatic brain injury.

At 05:57, Semikin reported that two people had been killed and 22 injured. Later, Fedorov reported 30 people had been injured, including a baby, a six-year-old boy and a 16-year-old girl.

Quote from Semikin: "The enemy launched strikes on the city. A house has been destroyed and a five-storey building has been partially destroyed.

High-rise residential buildings, houses, cars and a transport infrastructure facility have been damaged."

Background: Russian forces launched strikes on Zaporizhzhia on the evening of 23 November, injuring six people.

articles.title: Russian drone enters Poland during attack on Ukraine but is not shot down
articles.summary:
Poland has activated its air defence forces on the night of 24 November in response to a Russian attack on Ukraine.

Source: Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces on X (Twitter)

Quote: "In connection with strikes carried out by the Russian Federation against targets on Ukrainian territory using airborne weapons, the appropriate forces and assets of Poland's air defence system have been deployed."

Details: The command noted that these measures are precautionary and aimed at protecting Polish airspace, particularly in areas bordering those under threat.

The command added that it is continuously monitoring the situation and that forces under its command are on standby to respond immediately.

Update: The command later added that a Russian drone had violated Polish airspace during the attack on Ukraine's west. However, the Polish military did not open fire, saying that doing so could have posed a threat to civilians.

Quote: "The situation was continuously monitored and authorisation was given to destroy the object. After the UAV changed course eastwards, taking into account the potential threat to civilians and the possible consequences of shooting down the object, a decision was made to refrain from using weapons due to the risk of causing harm."

articles.title: Libya describes Ukrainian attack on Russian vessels as tantamount to declaration of war
articles.summary:
Musa Al-Koni, a member of Libya's Presidential Council, has condemned Ukraine's attack on the port of Benghazi, describing it as tantamount to a declaration of war against Libya. The country's Foreign Ministry has warned that such attacks pose a direct threat to Libya's national security.

Source: Libyan News Agency, citing a statement by Al-Koni; statement by Libya's Foreign Ministry

Details: Al-Koni held Ukraine fully responsible for these actions, described them as "terrorist" and noted that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had acknowledged them and even boasted about them.

The Libyan official described these actions as tantamount to a declaration of war against the Libyan state.

Quote from Al-Koni: "We will immediately begin taking all necessary legal and diplomatic measures – both regionally and internationally – to hold those responsible for violating Libyan sovereignty and threatening peace and security accountable. This includes referring the matter to the International Court of Justice, the UN Security Council, and other relevant organisations, in order to safeguard the rights of the Libyan state and its citizens through all legitimate means."

Details: Al-Koni called on the UN Security Council to convene an emergency meeting to address these developments, place Zelenskyy on a terrorism watchlist and take the necessary urgent measures to put an end to these aggressive actions.

Meanwhile, Libya's Foreign Ministry stated that it will not allow Libyan ports and civilian infrastructure facilities to be used for military purposes.

Quote from Libya's Foreign Ministry: "The continuation of the Russian-Ukrainian conflict does not grant any party the right to extend its military operations into Libyan territory or use Libya's sovereign domain as an arena for settling scores, in violation of the principles of the United Nations Charter and relevant rules of international law."

Background:

Two Libyan officials previously told the Associated Press that the Russian corvette Merkury had suffered serious damage as a result of a strike on a naval base in Benghazi, and a fire broke out at the base. Citing an initial investigation, AP wrote that the ship may have been hit by Ukrainian naval drones.

Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukrainian naval drones had sunk the Russian corvette Merkury, which had a Ka-27 helicopter on board, and also struck the dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Russia was using to transport weapons, near the Libyan port of Benghazi.

articles.title: Tajikistan withdrew from International Criminal Court on day Putin visited
articles.summary:
Tajikistan has announced that it withdrew from the International Criminal Court (ICC) on the same day that Russian leader Vladimir Putin visited the country.

Source: Le Monde, as reported by European Pravda

Details: Tajikistan has published an official notice announcing its withdrawal from the Rome Statute, stating that the decision took effect on 20 November 2026 – the day of Putin's visit. ICC member states are required to arrest Putin if he enters their territory.

Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova, Russia's commissioner for children's rights, have been wanted by the ICC since 2023 for the unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children. The Kremlin leader visited Tajikistan on his way back from a summit with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

In a statement, the ICC said it regrets Tajikistan's decision: "Decisions by States Parties to disengage from the Rome Statute risk undermining the collective pursuit of justice and weakening global efforts to end impunity. The ICC stands at the heart of the international system of accountability, and its effectiveness depends on sustained and unequivocal support from the international community."

Background:

In September 2023, the European Parliament called on the ICC to issue an arrest warrant against self-proclaimed Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko in connection with the deportation of Ukrainian children.

At the meeting in Shenzhen on 19 November, Trump urged Putin and Xi to join efforts to fight the ICC.

articles.title: Russia preparing new strikes on Ukraine, Zelenskyy says
articles.summary:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, citing intelligence reports, that Russia is preparing to carry out new strikes on Ukraine.

Source: Zelenskyy in his evening address on 23 November

Quote: "We have intelligence indicating that the Russians are preparing new strikes. Please heed missile threat alerts and stay safe."

Details: Zelenskyy also said he had held a meeting of the Staff of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief which focused on protecting Ukraine against Russian jet-powered drones in 2026 and 2027. The president said intelligence had provided detailed information about the scale of Russian production, schemes to obtain components, and plans to use Shahed drones.

Quote: "Countering this requires sanctions and real export controls – certainly stronger than those currently in place in some countries – and, of course, our own means of shooting down Shaheds. F-16s – Ukraine needs more of these aircraft. We will also need more Gripens, which are expected to arrive in Ukraine from January."

Details: The president also thanked Security Service of Ukraine personnel and units of the defence forces for a successful operation off the coast of Libya targeting two Russian vessels – one of Russia's newest corvettes and a cargo ship that was transporting weapons.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: Intelligence shows scale of Russian plans for jet-powered drone production – countermeasures are needed
articles.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that at a meeting of the Staff of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief on 23 November, he and other officials discussed ways to protect against Russian jet-powered drones, given the scale at which Russia plans to produce them.

Source: Zelenskyy in his evening address

Quote: "Today, I held a Staff meeting focused on essentially one issue – protection against Russian jet-powered drones this year and next, taking into account Russia's production plans.

We have details from our intelligence agencies, and we understand the scale of Russian production, the schemes they use to obtain components, and their plans for using Shaheds against us. Countering this requires sanctions and real export controls – certainly stronger than those currently in place in some countries – and, of course, our own means of shooting down Shaheds.

F-16s – Ukraine needs more of these aircraft. We will also need more Gripens, which are expected to arrive in Ukraine from January."

Details: Zelenskyy said there will be more aircraft for Ukraine's defence, and there is good news from Ukrainian weapons manufacturers regarding interceptors designed to counter jet-powered Shahed drones.

articles.title: EU companies to be barred from helping Russia repair oil refineries
articles.summary:
The European Commission has proposed banning European companies from helping Russia repair its energy infrastructure, including oil refineries, as part of the 22nd sanctions package.

Source: the Kyiv Independent, citing proposals presented by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on 23 November

Details: The energy services ban is intended to limit the ability of European businesses to help Russia repair damaged infrastructure. It comes as Ukrainian strikes continue to target Russian oil refineries, disrupting their operations and restricting Russia's export capacity.

"There cannot be business as usual in our economic relations with Russia," von der Leyen said.

She stressed that the EU will continue to propose new sanctions until Moscow demonstrates a genuine willingness to achieve a lasting peace in Ukraine.

The restrictions have not yet been adopted. The European Commission's proposals must be reviewed and unanimously approved by EU member states.

Background: On 23 November, the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery in Russia's Rostov Oblast suspended operations following a combined missile and drone attack. The regional governor reported the shutdown.

articles.title: German chancellor says 2008 decision not to admit Ukraine to NATO was a mistake
articles.summary:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said that the allies' decision not to offer Ukraine a Membership Action Plan (MAP) at the 2008 Bucharest NATO Summit was a mistake.

Source: Merz at a joint press conference with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Berlin on 23 November, as reported by DPA and European Pravda

Quote: "Today, looking back, we can all see what a mistake it was not to support the American proposal at the 2008 NATO summit in Bucharest to admit Ukraine to NATO. If it had become a member of NATO, this war could probably have been prevented."

Details: Merz's statement comes as French President Emmanuel Macron proposes to reopen discussions on Ukraine joining NATO.

"In the current situation, given Russia's hardline stance, I think we need to reopen the question of Ukraine's accession to NATO," Macron said after the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin.

Merz called France's position "logical", saying it is consistent with the security guarantees Ukraine needs and is expected to receive after the war ends. These include the idea of providing Ukraine with guarantees similar to those in Article 5 of the NATO Treaty. The German chancellor said such security guarantees are "very close" to NATO membership.

"Frankly, I cannot imagine Ukraine's future without the security guarantees it urgently needs. And these are security guarantees not only for Ukraine, but for all of us," Merz said.

Former German chancellor Angela Merkel has repeatedly defended her decision to refuse Ukraine a Membership Action Plan in 2008. She has argued that if Ukraine had started moving towards NATO membership, the war would have begun much earlier.

Background:

On 21 November, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that the issue of NATO membership for Ukraine continues to be raised at meetings with allies, but the outcome will depend on the terms on which the war ends.

Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had privately told his Western counterparts that he doubts the war in Ukraine can be ended through negotiations and doubts Kyiv will be able to join NATO in the near future.

articles.title: Russians repeatedly changed date and cause of Ukrainian journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna's death in state registers
articles.summary:
Data on the death of Ukrainian journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna, who died in Russian captivity, was amended several times in the register of Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat), with a different date or cause of death given each time.

Source: an investigation by Russian media outlet Vazhnye Istorii (Important Stories), based on leaked Rosstat data provided to the journalists by the hacker groups Silent Crow and Cyber Partisans

Details: The journalists found one record in the Rosstat database concerning the death of a woman whose dates of birth and death exactly match those of Viktoriia Roshchyna. The cause of death was determined by a forensic medical examiner, while the death was registered by a specialised department of the Civil Registry Office of the Perm city administration.

The outlet noted that a week before her death, Viktoriia was transferred from pre-trial detention centre No. 2 in Taganrog to pre-trial detention centre No. 3 in the city of Kizel in Perm Krai.

The register entry relating to the journalist's death was amended several times. The data was first entered in the Rosstat database in late December 2024, giving 16 December 2024 as the date of death and listing the cause as unknown. However, the death certificate issued was final rather than an interim one.

A few days later, the Civil Registry Office sent Rosstat a correction changing the date of death to 19 September 2024. If this date is accurate, Viktoriia died six days before the prisoner exchange in which she had been promised a place.

Amendments continued to be made in 2025. In February, a Rosstat employee entered details from a new death certificate and changed the cause of death from "unknown" to "illness". According to the latest approved information in the database, the journalist died of myocardial dystrophy – changes in the heart muscle that led to a heart rhythm disorder and pulmonary oedema.

The record was last amended on 11 February 2025, three days before Viktoriia's body was brought back to Ukraine.

The investigative journalists noted that when the cause of death is unknown, an interim death certificate is usually issued first. In Viktoriia's case, however, the first certificate was final. It was later replaced with a new one "in place of the final certificate", specifying a particular cause of death. Fewer than 0.3% of all records in the Rosstat system are amended in this way.

It is even rarer for the date of death to be changed to an earlier one, with both the day and month altered: this occurs in approximately 0.1% of records.

Meanwhile, other identifying details – citizenship, address, place of birth, marital status, education and occupation – are not listed in the record. Nor are they recorded in entries for other Ukrainians who have died in Russian custody, including Oleksandr Markov, a 74-year-old pensioner from Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Viktor Demchenko, a 71-year-old resident of Donetsk Oblast, and prisoner of war Oleksandr Ishchenko.

The journalists said the Russian authorities registered the death of Polish citizen Krzysztof Galos in the same way. Galos was detained in Russian-occupied territory of Ukraine in 2023 and held at pre-trial detention centre No. 2 in Taganrog. In all the identified cases except Ishchenko's, where the cause of death could not be established due to decomposition of the tissue, the forensic medical examiners listed heart and vascular diseases as the cause of death.

The place of death for Roshchyna, Markov, Ishchenko and Galos is listed in the database as "other location", which is the usual designation for deaths that occur in pre-trial detention centres or during transfers. The Ukrainian forensic medical examiners who examined Viktoriia's body found signs of torture, evidence of extreme emaciation, and some internal organs missing.

Read more: The Viktoriia Project: the story of the captivity and torture endured by journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna and thousands of Ukrainians imprisoned by Russia

Background:

In March 2022, Russian occupying forces abducted journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna for the first time in the occupied city of Berdiansk, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, and held her captive for 10 days. She was released on 21 March after being forced to record a video saying she had no complaints against the Russian secret services.

In August 2023, Viktoriia travelled to temporarily occupied territory again to prepare a report. She went missing on 3 August.

In May 2024, Serhii Tomilenko, head of the National Union of Journalists of Ukraine, reported that Russia had for the first time acknowledged Viktoriia's unlawful detention. The journalist's father had received a letter dated 17 April from the Russian Defence Ministry stating that Viktoriia was being held in Russia.

On 10 October 2024, Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War reported Roshchyna's death in Russian captivity.

Investigative journalists from Slidstvo.Info found that Viktoriia had been brutally tortured with electric shocks and a knife at Russian pre-trial detention centre No. 2 in Taganrog. Due to extreme emaciation, she weighed around 30 kg (66 lb). Shortly before her death she was transferred to pre-trial detention centre No. 3 in Kizel. Ukrainska Pravda reported that when the occupying forces returned Viktoriia's body, it was labelled as that of an "unidentified male" and some internal organs were missing, including the brain, eyeballs and part of the trachea.

On 14 May 2025, the Verkhovna Rada (Ukrainian parliament) backed a request from 26 MPs to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that Viktoriia Roshchyna be posthumously awarded the title of Hero of Ukraine.

On 14 July 2026, Ukrainska Pravda published an open appeal by media professionals, human rights activists and public figures calling for Viktoriia to be awarded the title of Hero of Ukraine. At the end of the month, nearly 800 signatures were submitted to the President's Office.

On 15 October, the Verkhovna Rada voted by 255 votes to resubmit the request to the president to posthumously award Viktoriia the title of Hero of Ukraine.

On 28 October, Viktoriia was posthumously honoured with an OXI Courage Award in Washington.

articles.title: NATO strengthens protection after Russian missiles violate Polish airspace
articles.summary:
NATO airborne early warning aircraft have been deployed to help protect Polish airspace following an incident involving Russian Kh-101 missiles.

Source: Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz on X (Twitter), as reported by European Pravda

Details: Kosiniak-Kamysz said the aircraft have been provided by Poland's NATO allies.

Quote: "Allied early warning aircraft are already bolstering the defence of Polish airspace. This is a response to recent incidents and a demonstration of NATO's commitments to Poland. We are seeking further support."

Details: Kosiniak-Kamysz said the aircraft are an important addition to ground-based air defence systems, Polish F-16s and fighter jets from NATO member states.

Background:

On 20 November, three Russian missiles violated Polish airspace during a large-scale Russian attack on Ukraine.

Debris from Kh-101 cruise missiles was found at three locations: Nowy Lipowiec in Lublin Voivodeship, and Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz in Podkarpackie Voivodeship.

On 21 November, Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski announced that the government would express its "extreme displeasure" to Russia over the breach of Polish airspace. He added that the issue would also be "discussed in Brussels, in both military and political circles".

articles.title: Russia accuses Estonia of allowing Ukrainian drones to use its airspace
articles.summary:
Russia's Foreign Ministry has accused Estonia of assisting Ukraine by supposedly allowing Ukrainian forces to use its airspace.

Source: Russian Foreign Ministry on Telegram, as reported by European Pravda

Details: The Russian Foreign Ministry claimed that Estonia is "deliberately and purposefully providing its airspace" to Ukrainian forces so that they could fly their drones through Estonian territory.

"Estonia continues to actively support the Kyiv regime by covertly providing its airspace for Ukrainian drones to fly through in order to carry out attacks on north-western Russia," the ministry said.

It also claimed that all facts and evidence of Estonia's complicity in supporting Ukraine had "been documented repeatedly".

Background:

Earlier on 23 November, Russia's Foreign Ministry summoned Marek Ühtegi, Estonia's chargé d'affaires in Russia, to lodge a strong protest over the decision to close crossing points on the Russian-Estonian border from 1 December.

The decision to close the border was made after Russian military intelligence organised an attempted act of sabotage at Threod Systems, an Estonian defence industry company that produces reconnaissance and combat drones.

Estonia has repeatedly insisted that it does not allow Ukraine to use its airspace for drone flights.

articles.title: UK defence secretary wants to find out what happened with Starlink and Starshield in Ukraine
articles.summary:
UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has said that disruptions to the Starlink and Starshield satellite systems in Ukraine require a clear explanation, as they have seriously undermined the trust of allies.

Source: European Pravda, citing Streeting's briefing in Kyiv as reported by Ukrainian news agency Ukrinform

Details: The UK official stressed that such outages in the Starlink and Starshield systems seriously erode trust.

Quote: "On Starlink and Starshield, we do need to get to the bottom of what has happened and how and why the service interruption has occurred. And I can tell you that this has been a topic of conversation among defence ministers right across Europe. It has really dented confidence and trust."

Details: Streeting insisted that allies must be given a clear account of the communications outages, including how and why they occurred.

Background:

On 12 November, Zelenskyy said that the Ukrainian military had been experiencing significant disruptions to Starshield for several days.

He later said SpaceX told the Ukrainian Defence Ministry that it has not imposed any restrictions on Starshield operations and that the problem is technical in nature.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump claimed he had not heard about restrictions on Starlink operations in Ukraine.
